🍎 Lesson plan · 🤿 Deep dive · Lesson 10

Lesson plan: Creative AI

How AI makes pictures, music and stories, how a picture appears out of noise, and the questions it raises.

By the end of the lesson, students can

  • explain that generative AI learns patterns from examples and uses them to make something new;
  • describe, as an intuition, how a diffusion model turns noise into a picture, step by step;
  • discuss consent, copyright, labels and deepfakes, and use AI as an honest creative partner.

Warm-up

Imagine a picture of a cat astronaut, painted in watercolour. Could you tell whether a person or an AI made it? How?

Collect ideas; many old “tells” no longer work. Keep the question open for the discussion about labels and watermarks.

Reading

Students read the lesson “Creative AI”. Students look for how a diffusion model makes a picture, what a GAN is, and the story of the Pope's puffer jacket.

Activity: Mini-lab “From noise to picture”

  1. Students open the mini-lab in lesson 10 and pick a prompt.
  2. They press “Remove noise” one step at a time and, after each step, describe what they see.
  3. They press “New noise”, play all the steps again with the same prompt, and compare the two pictures.
  4. Pairs read the note under the mini-lab and explain how a real diffusion model is different from this illustration.

For students who finish early

Fast finishers write a picture prompt in layers (the subject, a style, the light or mood, the details) and explain what each layer would change.

Discussion questions

  • Is it fair to train image generators on artists' work without asking them? What would be fairer?
  • Should every AI-made picture carry a label or a watermark? Who should check?
  • When you show work that AI helped with, how should you say so?
  • Why was the picture of the Pope in a puffer jacket a warning, even though it was a joke?

Exit ticket

Write one question you would ask before sharing a surprising picture.

Quick check. Some AI image tools hide an invisible mark in every picture they make. What is it for?
Right answer: To show later that the picture was made by AI

Easier and harder

Easier. Run the mini-lab on the projector: the class calls out what they see after each step, and you write the words on the board.

Harder. Students compare a GAN (the forger and the detective) with a diffusion model (removing noise) in a short paragraph: what each network does, and how it learns.
